FailureFeatures.description:
Structured diagnostic evidence attached to an ``ok=false`` envelope on operation failure.

Captures *why* an operation may have failed, independent of *what* failed: the
feature set a diagnosis would need, not an enumeration of failure modes. Every
field is optional and populated only where the operation can supply it (so a
bare ``{}`` is a valid, if uninformative, block). This layer produces evidence;
it does not decide recovery. See issue #230.

error_class_raw.description: The failure signature exactly as the producer (a failing op or a caller-supplied probe hook) wrote it. Open, ungoverned, preserved verbatim — the framework cannot enforce a vocabulary across producers it does not own, and never rejects or rewrites this value. Used for audit and as the input to normalization.
error_class_raw.title: Error Class Raw

error_class.description: The canonical failure class, assigned by the framework's normalizer at ingest (NOT written by the producer) by mapping 'error_class_raw' onto a controlled, framework-owned vocabulary. This is the field deterministic recovery policy and the recall/memory subsystem index on, so it MUST come from a value space the framework governs. 'unknown' means the normalizer could not canonicalize the raw string — that is the well-defined trigger to escalate to a decision-maker (e.g. the agentic layer), whose resolution should feed a new raw->canonical mapping back into the normalizer rather than minting a new free-text class. The enum is the starter vocabulary; it grows via schema-version bumps, which is the single governed place the vocabulary changes. Distinct from the envelope's coarser 'error_code' — several error_classes can map to one error_code. MUST stay aligned with the 'error_class' field in failures.output.json (same vocabulary, same normalizer).
error_class.title: Error Class

resource_spec.description: The resource/sweep spec in effect at the moment of failure (e.g. GPU type/count, scheduler-level params, sampling width). The discriminator that turns a shared signature into opposite fixes — e.g. OOM at tp_size=2 vs OOM at n=128.
resource_spec.title: Resource Spec

probes.description: Optional targeted probe outputs from caller-supplied probe hooks.

FailureFeatures.title: FailureFeatures

_TemporalContext.description: When in the operation's life did it fail — the single most discriminating feature (structural vs. runtime).

phase.description: 'first_attempt' = failed before any unit of work succeeded (points at a structural/config problem). 'after_progress' = failed after N units succeeded (points at a runtime/data-dependent problem). 'unknown' when the operation cannot tell.
phase.title: Phase

successful_units.description: Count of units (tasks, requests, rounds) that succeeded before the failure, when known.
successful_units.title: Successful Units

_TemporalContext.title: _TemporalContext

_AttemptsThisEpisode.description: What recovery has already been tried in this failure episode — lets a decision-maker avoid re-trying an exhausted strategy.

count.description: Number of recovery attempts already made this episode.
count.title: Count

strategies.description: Ordered list of recovery strategies already applied (e.g. 'retry', 'resubmit', 'restart_service', 'increase_walltime').

_AttemptsThisEpisode.title: _AttemptsThisEpisode

_LivenessVsCorrectness.description: Distinguishes 'down' from 'up-but-broken' by separating a liveness signal (does it respond?) from a correctness signal (does a real request return a valid result?). The classic silent-rot case is liveness=pass, correctness=fail.

liveness.description: Result of a liveness check (port open / process alive / health endpoint).
liveness.title: Liveness

correctness.description: Result of a real-path request (an actual request that exercises the backing work, not a port ping).
correctness.title: Correctness

_LivenessVsCorrectness.title: _LivenessVsCorrectness

_LogTail.description: Bounded, normalized tail of the relevant log. Callers MUST bound this (the schema does not transport unbounded logs) and SHOULD normalize volatile tokens (timestamps, paths, addresses) so signatures cluster.

truncated.description: True when content was dropped to fit the bound.
truncated.title: Truncated

source.description: Where the tail came from, e.g. 'stderr', 'task.log', 'service.stdout'.
source.title: Source

_LogTail.title: _LogTail

_Probe.description: One targeted probe result from a caller-supplied probe hook.
_Probe.title: _Probe
